tldr: Headlines across all 17 buckets default to the progressive-versus-establishment frame, but a distinct secondary layer — naming AIPAC outright at the headline level — separates Russia, pan-Arab, Iranian state, and Intercept coverage from the rest. France 24 Spanish and the Jerusalem Post uniquely foreground identity (Muslim doctor; Jewish Democratic reckoning) rather than the party-direction contest.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to deploy 'extremist' and 'Muslim Brotherhood' in a single title, invoking security and criminal-threat language absent from every other outlet in the corpus at the headline layer.

Only headline foregrounding post-primary party unification ('Establishment Dems Fall In Line') rather than the primary result itself — the only outlet to make the establishment's rapid rally the headline story.

Only headline framing El-Sayed's win as a symptom of dual-populism dynamics ('gli opposti populismi') rather than a progressive-vs-establishment contest — a structural interpretation absent from all Anglophone headlines.

Only headline posing a prescriptive lesson-drawing question ('What the Democrats must learn') rather than reporting the result — signals editorial concern about Democratic strategy rather than factual coverage of the primary outcome.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, AIPAC is named outright by three geopolitically opposed non-Western outlets (RT, Middle East Eye, Tehran Times) and The Intercept, establishing foreign-lobby money as a rival axis to the universal progressive-vs-establishment frame that dominates every other bucket.
